definition: bring oneself into favor through flattery or effort to please
memoryTip: In + graces: flattery to get into someone’s good graces.
correctPassage: He tried to ingratiate himself with the new director through constant flattery.
wrongPassages: She managed to ingratiate the entire board by insulting each member in turn.
His plan to ingratiate the budget cut was to ignore every request for funding.
They ingratiated the angry crowd by refusing to answer questions at all.

definition: excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters
memoryTip: A garrulous guest pours a garbled river of endless small talk.
correctPassage: A garrulous seatmate made the long flight feel even longer.
wrongPassages: The garrulous hermit went years without speaking to another person.
Her garrulous reply was a single nod and then complete silence.
Judges praised the garrulous witness who answered only yes or no.

memoryTip: Fervor on fire — fervid means passion running hot.
correctPassage: Fervid supporters filled the square hours before the speech.
wrongPassages: His fervid reaction was a shrug and a muttered “whatever.”
The crowd stayed fervid by leaving early and barely clapping.
She gave a fervid presentation in a flat monotone that put half the room to sleep.

memoryTip: Exigent = emergency-urgent — it demands attention now.
correctPassage: Exigent circumstances justified the emergency order.
wrongPassages: The exigent memo could wait until next fiscal year without any harm.
They labeled the optional survey exigent and told staff to ignore it.
His exigent vacation plans involved no deadlines and no time pressure at all.

definition: understood by only a small specialist group
memoryTip: Eso-teric: for the inner circle only — specialist knowledge.
correctPassage: The seminar covers esoteric topics rarely taught to undergraduates.
wrongPassages: The esoteric flyer used words every kindergartner already knew by heart.
They called the national anthem esoteric because the whole stadium sang along.
Her esoteric cooking show explained only how to boil water for pasta.

memoryTip: E-nerve-ate: strip the nerve/energy out — weaken (not energize!).
correctPassage: Heat and humidity can enervate even seasoned hikers.
wrongPassages: A cold shower and strong coffee will enervate you for the morning run.
The coach’s speech was meant to enervate the team into a furious comeback.
They hoped the rest day would enervate sore muscles back to full strength.

memoryTip: Belli- (war) + gerent — warlike and ready to fight.
correctPassage: A belligerent tone in the letter made negotiation unlikely.
wrongPassages: His belligerent handshake and warm smile put every guest at ease.
The mediator stayed belligerent by refusing to raise her voice or take sides.
They praised the belligerent cease-fire that ended every dispute without a threat.

definition: wanting or devouring great quantities of something
memoryTip: Vora = devour — a huge appetite for food, books, or work.
correctPassage: A voracious reader, she finished several novels each week.
wrongPassages: His voracious appetite was satisfied by half a cracker and a sip of water.
The voracious archive held only one short pamphlet no one ever opened.
She was a voracious student who never finished a single assigned chapter.

definition: a change of circumstances, often unwelcome
memoryTip: Vici-change: the ups and downs fortune throws at you.
correctPassage: The firm survived every vicissitude of the market cycle.
wrongPassages: Life under the monarchy was one long vicissitude of perfect, unchanging calm.
They planned for vicissitude by freezing every policy for the next decade.
The lake’s vicissitude meant the waterline never rose or fell by an inch.

definition: looking or sounding sad and dismal
memoryTip: Lugubrious funeral face — exaggeratedly mournful and gloomy.
correctPassage: A lugubrious soundtrack made the short film feel longer than it was.
wrongPassages: His lugubrious welcome was a bright grin and a round of cheerful jokes.
The parade stayed lugubrious with confetti, brass bands, and dancing crowds.
She delivered a lugubrious toast that left the room laughing for minutes.
